instruction: Get claim-to-DeepProbLog compilation working. Compare syntax plus role labeling and rule/neural transformation, direct semantic parsing plus post-processing, and suitable alternatives. Research predicate/logical-form generation, run experiments, and update the plan/checklist before media verification.
scope: Practical claim-to-logical-form front ends and deterministic DeepProbLog compilation
sub_questions: What do trained SRL and AMR preserve?
How are logical scope and predicates generated?
How should a small frozen model generate a logical form?
How do we distinguish validity from meaning preservation?

papers.title: Wide-Coverage Semantic Analysis with Boxer
papers.problem: How to obtain broad-coverage formal meaning from syntax.
papers.method: CCG parsing feeds compositional construction of discourse representation structures, which can be translated to first-order logic.
papers.results: Describes an operational semantic-analysis pipeline. No result is transferred to AViD.
papers.relevance: Syntax is useful when paired with a defined compositional semantics; a dependency edge is not itself a logical operator.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: ccg2lambda: A Compositional Semantics System
papers.authors: Pascual Martínez-Gómez, Koji Mineshima, Yusuke Miyao, Daisuke Bekki
papers.problem: How to compute logical forms from syntactic derivations.
papers.method: Assign typed semantic templates to CCG categories and compose them with lambda-calculus operations.
papers.results: Implements compositional semantics and theorem-proving applications.
papers.relevance: A principled syntax-to-logic baseline is possible, but installing CCG and supplying lexical templates is additional work; it is not our current UD rules.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Abstract Meaning Representation for Sembanking
papers.problem: A sentence-level semantic representation less tied to surface syntax.
papers.method: Represent concepts, semantic roles, names and shared referents as a rooted graph.
papers.results: Introduces the representation and annotation effort.
papers.relevance: Provides a standard intermediate representation and pretrained parsers; not a complete executable specification of all English meanings.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Expressive Power of Abstract Meaning Representations
papers.problem: What AMR means in formal logic, particularly with negation and shared variables.
papers.method: Define a recursive translation to first-order logic and discuss extensions for scope and projection.
papers.results: Gives formal results about expressiveness and a scope-aware translation.
papers.relevance: Do not simply conjoin every AMR triple or assume every embedded event is asserted. Our restricted translation is not an implementation of the complete formal account.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Universal Decompositional Semantics on Universal Dependencies
papers.authors: Aaron Steven White, Drew Reisinger, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Tim Vieira, Sheng Zhang, Rachel Rudinger, Kyle Rawlins, Benjamin Van Durme
papers.problem: How to anchor predicate/argument structures and semantic annotations in dependencies.
papers.method: Build a dependency-based predicate/argument layer for decompositional semantic annotation.
papers.results: Introduces a representation and annotation framework.
papers.relevance: An existing extraction baseline is preferable to repeatedly rebuilding local dependency heuristics. Extraction does not define source or quantifier scope.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: An Evaluation of PredPatt and Open IE via Stage 1 Semantic Role Labeling
papers.authors: Sheng Zhang, Rachel Rudinger, Benjamin Van Durme
papers.problem: How predicate/argument extraction compares with SRL-oriented evaluation.
papers.method: Evaluate PredPatt and Open IE using a semantic-role-labeling framework.
papers.results: Reports an extraction evaluation; no universal claim of logical completeness.
papers.relevance: Useful as an inexpensive argument-span diagnostic; preserving phrases alone does not expose every learnable binding.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Annotation of Tense and Aspect Semantics for Sentential AMR
papers.authors: Lucia Donatelli, Michael Regan, William Croft, Nathan Schneider
papers.problem: Standard AMR omits temporal distinctions important for inference.
papers.method: Augment finite predications with temporal and aspectual distinctions.
papers.relevance: Add source-aligned tense/aspect to AMR; landed and is landing must not collapse. This does not locate a video event.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: One SPRING to Rule Them Both: Symmetric AMR Semantic Parsing and Generation without a Complex Pipeline
papers.authors: Michele Bevilacqua, Rexhina Blloshmi, Roberto Navigli
papers.problem: How to parse/generate AMR without a complex pipeline.
papers.method: Use a pretrained encoder-decoder model with a graph linearization and pointer tokens.
papers.results: Shows strong AMR parsing/generation performance and examines distribution shift.
papers.relevance: A task-trained encoder-decoder is a practical alternative to prompting a general decoder. Our amrlib BART checkpoint uses parse_xfm, not SPRING weights.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Constrained Language Models Yield Few-Shot Semantic Parsers
papers.problem: How to bootstrap semantic parsing with few examples.
papers.method: Use constrained generation of an English-like controlled language with a deterministic mapping to logical forms.
papers.results: Demonstrates effective few-shot parsing on several community tasks.
papers.relevance: A small readable target language is an alternative to a large token-indexed JSON schema; its meaning still needs checking.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: PICARD: Parsing Incrementally for Constrained Auto-Regressive Decoding from Language Models
papers.authors: Torsten Scholak, Nathan Schucher, Dzmitry Bahdanau
papers.problem: Autoregressive decoders can generate invalid formal expressions.
papers.method: Reject inadmissible next tokens using incremental parsing.
papers.relevance: Grammar-constrained decoding can address formatting, but cannot guarantee correct roles, polarity or source scope. We have not implemented it in this run.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models for Natural Language to First-Order Logic Translation
papers.authors: Yuan Yang, Siheng Xiong, Ali Payani, Ehsan Shareghi, Faramarz Fekri
papers.problem: Reliable NL-to-FOL translation and suitable evaluation data.
papers.method: Construct MALLS using generated pairs, parsing, human annotation and filtering; train specialized translators and correction models.
papers.results: Presents 28K NL/FOL pairs and translation experiments.
papers.relevance: Off-the-shelf logical translators exist. Their quantified-rule datasets and predicate vocabularies differ from AViD event descriptions; check transfer before adopting or fine-tuning.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Learning Semantic Structure through First-Order-Logic Translation
papers.problem: Whether language models attach predicates to the right objects.
papers.method: Compare question answering and FOL translation using prompting and fine-tuning on synthetic examples.
papers.results: Finds predicate/argument confusions and benefits from FOL-oriented supervision in its settings.
papers.relevance: Directly supports testing role swaps and modifier attachment; valid formulas alone do not certify those bindings.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Divide and Translate: Compositional First-Order Logic Translation and Verification for Complex Logical Reasoning
papers.authors: Hyun Ryu, Gyeongman Kim, Hyemin S. Lee, Eunho Yang
papers.problem: Complex logical meaning is hard to translate in one generation.
papers.method: Parse component/dependency structures, translate progressively, and compare alternative formulas using a solver.
papers.relevance: Clause-by-clause translation is a stronger next experiment than expanding one monolithic prompt. Solver agreement is not proof of faithfulness to a media claim.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: Few-Shot Natural Language to First-Order Logic Translation via Code Generation
papers.problem: How to generate complex logical forms without task-specific fine-tuning.
papers.method: Use in-context learning and progressive code generation as an intermediate representation.
papers.results: Reports improvements over training-free translation baselines.
papers.relevance: Supports testing a short structured construction interface; never execute arbitrary model-generated Python in our compiler.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: NL2LOGIC: AST-Guided Translation of Natural Language into First-Order Logic with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Rizky Ramadhana Putra, Raihan Sultan Pasha Basuki, Yutong Cheng, Peng Gao
papers.problem: Fragile syntax and low semantic faithfulness in text-to-logic translation.
papers.method: Recursively parse clauses into an abstract syntax tree; deterministically generate solver code.
papers.results: Evaluates syntax, semantics and downstream reasoning separately on FOLIO, LogicNLI and ProofWriter.
papers.relevance: Very close precedent for separating semantic parsing from deterministic compilation. That separation alone cannot be our novelty; the future paper must establish the multimodal binding/evidence contribution.
papers.verification: Primary venue page or author PDF opened on 2026-10-28

papers.title: DeepProbLog: Neural Probabilistic Logic Programming
papers.authors: Robin Manhaeve, Sebastijan Dumančić, Angelika Kimmig, Thomas Demeester, Luc De Raedt
papers.problem: How to combine neural predictions and probabilistic logic.
papers.method: Neural predicates supply probabilities to ProbLog inference and differentiable learning.
papers.results: Demonstrates neural/symbolic inference and learning tasks.
papers.relevance: It is a backend, not an English semantic parser. A backend can faithfully execute a mistranslated claim.

themes: Semantic parsing and deterministic code generation are separate stages; DeepProbLog does not supply the former.
SRL supplies useful predicate/argument spans but not complete scope, coreference or noun-phrase semantics.
AMR provides roles and shared referents; its conversion to executable logic requires scope rules and additional tense/aspect information.
Constrained decoding improves validity. Semantic faithfulness needs separate reference judgments and contrastive checks.
Recent clause/AST-based translation is directly relevant and already established in prior work.

gaps.statement: Which front end preserves AViD source scope, roles, shared identities and tense with low development cost?
gaps.evidence: Our same-input comparison; none of the cited benchmark results answers this domain-specific question.

gaps.statement: Choose the level of decomposition explicitly: a source complement or noun phrase kept as one string is not a set of learned internal bindings.
gaps.evidence: PredPatt/SRL extraction versus AMR-FOL scope; source contents are still opaque in our current pilot.

gaps.statement: Use familiar parsing/compiler techniques as infrastructure; establish later novelty through multimodal evidence assignments and binding learning.
gaps.evidence: Boxer, ccg2lambda, CLOVER, Code4Logic and NL2LOGIC already separate meaning construction from formal execution.
